title: PRAKAS ON THE MAINTENACE OF MINIMUM RESERVE REQUIREMENT IN DEPOSIT-TAKING BANKS AND FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS
text:
Article 3.-
For the purposes of this Prakas, the following terms are defined as follows:
• Base period refers to the number of consecutive days during which the Institution
calculates deposits and other borrowings in KHR and foreign currencies to determine
the minimum reserve requirement to be maintained during the maintenance period.
• Maintenance period refers to the number of consecutive days during which the
Institution shall hold the reserve assets in KHR and foreign currencies to comply with
the daily compulsory thresholds and the minimum reserve requirements which have
been calculated during the base period.
• Average deposits and other borrowings refer to the total of deposits and other
borrowings amount reported during the base period divided by 42 for KHR and the total
of deposits and other borrowings amount reported during the base periods divided by
14 for foreign currencies. This average shall be used to determine the minimum
reserve requirements to be held during the corresponding maintenance period. The
average deposits and other borrowings shall be calculated separately for KHR and for
other foreign currencies in accordance with the Institution’s transactions.
• Reserve requirement rate refers to a rate set by the NBC that applies to the average
deposits and other borrowings, which are used to calculate the minimum reserve
requirement to be held, in average, over the corresponding maintenance period.
• Eligible assets held refers to amounts of reserve assets held, over the maintenance period
with the NBC, which are used to determine the average minimum reserve assets held.
• Average minimum reserve asset held refer to the reserve amount that shall be
maintained in the form of eligible assets with the NBC in compliance with the
requirements set forth in this Prakas. The average minimum reserve asset held in KHR
is calculated by adding the amounts of eligible assets held at the NBC during the 42
calendar days of the maintenance period divided by 42. The average minimum reserve
asset held in foreign currencies is calculated by adding the amounts of eligible assets
held at the NBC during the 14 calendar days of the maintenance period divided by 14.
The average minimum reserve asset held shall be calculated separately for KHR and
for other foreign currencies in accordance with the Institution’s transactions.
• Daily compulsory threshold refers to the determination of minimum reserve
requirement of at least 0% in KHR and at least 80% in foreign currencies to be
maintained every day over the maintenance period in the Institutions’ reserve
requirement accounts with the NBC.
• Minimum reserve requirements refer to amounts determined by multiplying the
applicable reserve requirement rate by the average deposits and other borrowings.
These amounts shall be calculated before the maintenance period and reported to the
NBC in a timely manner. Minimum reserve requirements are recalculated separately
every 42 calendar days for KHR and every 14 calendar days for foreign currencies.
Chapter 2
Reserve Requirements
Article 4.-
Reserve requirements are functioned as both a tool for monetary policy implementation and a
banking supervision requirement. Reserve requirement rates are subject to changes based
on policy needs and global economic circumstances. Reserve requirement rates are
determined in a separate regulation.
2

Reserve requirement shall apply to deposits and other borrowings namely deposits from both
resident and non-resident customers, deposits from non-resident banks and financial institutions,
and borrowings from non-residents, except for borrowings from non-residents with remaining
maturity over 3 years and subordinated debt that meet the criteria permitted for inclusion in
the calculation of regulatory capital or net worth.
Article 5.-
Institution shall establish and implement appropriate and prudent liquidity risk management
policies to comply with the requirements set forth in this Prakas.
Chapter 3
Eligible Assets Held Against Minimum Reserve Requirements
Article 6.-
Institution shall maintain, on average, sufficient balance of eligible assets held with the NBC
to comply with their minimum reserve requirements.
Article 7.-
Cash on hands is not considered as eligible assets held to comply with minimum reserve
requirement held.
Assets eligible for maintenance of reserve requirements are limited to:
• KHR: balances held with the NBC in the reserve requirement account and current
account denominated in KHR over the 42-day maintenance period, and;
• Foreign currencies: balances held with the NBC in the corresponding foreign
currencies reserve requirement accounts over the 14-day maintenance period.
Chapter 4
Base Period and Maintenance Period
Article 8.-
The reserve requirement calculation relies on two distinct periods, “base period” and
“maintenance period”.
Article 9.-
The base period for KHR is a 42-day calendar period which daily average deposits and other
borrowings, and for foreign currencies is a 14-day calendar period which daily average
deposits and other borrowings are subject to calculation for the minimum reserve requirements
and the daily compulsory thresholds and shall be reported to the NBC. The amounts of
minimum reserve requirement during the following maintenance period are determined by
multiplying the average deposits and other borrowings observed during the base period with
the applicable reserve requirement rates.
Article 10.-
The maintenance period starts on the fourth day after the last day of the base period.
The maintenance period is a 42-day calendar periods for reserve assets in KHR and 14-day
calendar period for reserve assets in foreign currencies, where the Institution shall maintain
eligible assets held in accordance with daily compulsory threshold on average every 42 days
and 14 days of the base period respectively. Furthermore, the Institution shall maintain
average minimum reserve assets held at the end of the maintenance period at least equal to
minimum reserve requirement calculated in the base period.
3

Chapter 5
Average Minimum Reserve Assets Held
Article 11.-
Since the eligible assets held with the NBC are averaged over the maintenance period, the
calculation of reserve requirement may allow flexibility. However, the Institution shall take
adequate measures to ensure compliance with the minimum threshold set forth in Article 14
of this Prakas.
The Institution is considered in compliance with this Prakas when the average amount of
eligible assets held over the maintenance period is at a minimum equal to at least 100% of
the minimum reserve requirement amount calculated based on the figures reported for the
preceding base period.
Article 12.-
The Institutions’ current account and reserve requirement account with positive balance and
denominated in KHR are considered as eligible assets for compliance with minimum reserve
requirement in KHR. The balance of current accounts and reserve requirement accounts shall
be added up daily over the maintenance period. The division between these balances with 42
shall be compared to the minimum reserve requirement amount, which was calculated in the
base period.
Article 13.-
Balances held in current accounts denominated in foreign currencies shall not be considered
as eligible assets held for compliance with minimum reserve requirements in foreign
currencies. Balance held in reserve requirement accounts in foreign currencies shall be added
up daily over the maintenance period and shall be divided by 14 to compare with the minimum
reserve requirement amount, which was calculated in the base period.
Chapter 6
Minimum Threshold of Reserve Held and Reserve Deficiencies
Article 14.-
For the purpose of calculating reserve requirement in the maintenance period, the Institution
shall maintain balance of the reserve requirement account in foreign currencies at the NBC
over the 14-day maintenance period of at least a daily compulsory threshold equal to 80% in
foreign currencies of the minimum reserve requirements calculated during the base period
and at least 100% at the end of maintenance period.
Although the NBC allows the Institution to maintain daily compulsory threshold of 0% in KHR
reserve requirements, the Institution shall calculate the average of sum of combined balances
in KHR of the Institution's reserve requirement account and current account at the NBC in
order to maintain a minimum reserve requirement amount of at least 100% at the end of the
maintenance period.
Article 15.-
Breaches of daily compulsory thresholds of 80% in foreign currencies and insufficient average
minimum reserve requirements for both KHR and foreign currencies over a given maintenance
period shall be considered reserve deficiencies and shall be liable to sanctions and
supervisory actions by the NBC against the contravening Institution.
4

Chapter 7
The Implementation and Reporting of Minimum Reserve Requirement Maintenance
Article 16.-
The Institution shall implement reserve requirement maintenance in KHR and foreign currencies
as instructed in separate schedule on base period and maintenance period.
Article 17.-
The Institution may use the excess reserve amount above the daily compulsory threshold of
0% in KHR over the 42-day maintenance period and 80% in foreign currencies over the 14-day
maintenance period. Nevertheless, the Institution shall maintain average minimum reserve
asset held at least 100% of the minimum reserve requirement in both KHR and foreign currencies,
calculated based on figures reported in base period at the end of the maintenance period.
Article 18.-
The Institution shall submit both base period and maintenance period reports as follows:
• Report of Base Period: The Institution shall submit base period report to the NBC within
3 (three) days after the end of base period. This report shall reflect daily balances of
deposit and other borrowings subject to reserve requirements, minimum reserve
requirements, minimum threshold 0% in KHR and 80% in foreign currencies and shall
be established separately for KHR and for each foreign currency. A table for base
period report is provided in Appendix of this Prakas;
• Report of Maintenance Period: The Institution shall submit maintenance period report
to the NBC within 3 (three) days after the end of maintenance period. This report shall
reflect daily balances of eligible assets held with the NBC and shall be reported
separately for KHR and for each foreign currency, which can verify the compliance with
the minimum thresholds of 0% in KHR and 80% in foreign currencies. A table of
maintenance period report is provided in Appendix of this Prakas.
Chapter 8
Sanctions and Fines
Article 19.-
In case the Institution fails to meet the daily compulsory threshold of 80% in foreign currency
reserve held, it shall incur a penalty charged with a daily rate calculated by converting Marginal
Lending Facilities (MLF) annual rate plus 5% on the shortfall amount (amount held in reserve
requirement account minus 80% of reserve requirement amount in foreign currency) on the
date of non-compliance. In the event of repeated deficiencies in consecutive periods, the
penalty rate shall increase to 4% per day.
Article 20.-
Deficiencies due to insufficient average reserve assets held over a given maintenance period
shall incur a penalty charged with a daily rate calculated by converting MLF annual rate plus
3% for reserve requirement held in KHR, and MLF annual rate plus 5% for reserve requirement
held in foreign currencies, on the shortfall amount (average minimum reserve assets held
minus minimum reserve requirement for the maintenance period). In case of repeated
deficiencies in consecutive periods, the penalty rate shall increase to 4% per day.
5

Article 21.-
Since breaching daily compulsory thresholds and reserve insufficiencies implies managerial
issues and/or potential liquidity issues, the NBC shall consider appropriate supervisory actions
to address the situation and exercise its sanctioning powers as stated in Article 52 of the Law
on Banking and Financial Institutions.
Chapter 9
Final Provisions
Article 22.-
Prakas N° B37-025-005 Prokor dated January 8, 2025 on the Maintenance of Minimum
Reserve Requirement in Banks and Financial Institutions and all provisions contrary to this
Prakas shall be repealed.
Article 23.-
The Secretary General, the Director General of Banking Supervision, the Director General of
Regulation and Financial Inclusion, the Director General of Policy and International Cooperation,
the Director General of Central Banking Operations, the Cashier General, the Director General
of Cash Management, the General Inspector, Directors of all relevant Departments and Units
in the National Bank of Cambodia and all Deposit-taking Banks and Financial Institutions
under the National Bank of Cambodia’s supervisory authority shall strictly implement this
Prakas.
Article 24.-
This Prakas shall have effect from the signing date.
